questions.q: Why does the lesson say a Salesforce admin portfolio matters more than it might for some other technical roles?
options: Because Salesforce orgs are always public by default
Because Trailhead already serves as a complete portfolio on its own
Because resumes are not allowed to mention Salesforce work
Because the real work usually lives inside a private org a reviewer can't just click into, unlike a public code repo
questions.explain: The lesson explains that a private Salesforce org can't be clicked into the way a public repo can, which is exactly why a narrative portfolio matters.

questions.q: What three things does the lesson say each portfolio section should answer?
options: What the problem was, what was built, and why that approach was chosen
The price, the vendor, and the release date
The exam objectives, the passing score, and the retake policy
The company name, the job title, and the salary
questions.explain: The lesson states each section should cover the business problem, what was built, and the reasoning behind the approach.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should a portfolio's automation section include alongside a screenshot of the Flow canvas?
options: A list of every Flow element type that exists in Salesforce
A certification exam score
The business trigger or manual process the automation replaced
The Apex equivalent of the same logic
questions.explain: The lesson specifically says to pair the Flow canvas screenshot with the business trigger that made the automation necessary.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about including live login credentials or an open org link in a portfolio?
options: It is required so reviewers can verify the work themselves
It should be avoided -- screenshots and a read-only walkthrough are enough
It is only a concern for Architect-level portfolios
It is fine as long as the org uses fictional data
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says not to publish live login credentials or an open-access org link, and that screenshots plus a read-only walkthrough are sufficient.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about where a portfolio needs to be hosted?
options: A single page -- a doc, a Notion page, a simple site, or a PDF -- is enough, as long as it's linked from your resume and Trailhead profile
Only on a custom-built website with a paid domain
It must be hosted directly inside the Salesforce org itself
Portfolios should never be linked from a resume
questions.explain: The lesson says a portfolio doesn't need to be elaborate -- a single linked page with clear screenshots and write-ups is enough.
